access_notes.value: API credentials are self-serve: keys are tied to a Clay user and workspace and created under API and CLI → API keys (UI, CLI, or agent plugin), with no approval or partner gate documented. Structured Tables queries are Enterprise-only.
access_notes.quote: API keys are tied to a Clay user and workspace access. Create one under API and CLI → API keys

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: URL path versioning (/public/v0); no deprecation or sunset policy found in the retrieved documentation.

verdict_reason: Clay publishes official developer docs and users create their own API keys in the Clay UI/CLI, with the Public API exposed as REST under /public/v0. The documented surface covers searches, routines, audiences/signals, webhooks, and Enterprise-only table queries, and Clay also operates a documented MCP server at https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp. No sales contact, partner approval, or app review is documented for obtaining Public API credentials; the main limitation is that structured table queries require an Enterprise plan.
open_questions: The fetched pricing page text in the bundle did not include plan details, so it could not be verified from official quotable text whether API access is included on a Free plan or only via trial/paid tiers; search snippets suggested API/CLI on all plans but snippets are not citable.
Rate limits and quotas were not found in the retrieved developer docs; confirm limits before building.
No official vendor SDKs were listed in the docs index; only the Clay CLI and agent plugin are documented, so SDK availability is unconfirmed.
Sandbox mode docs appeared in search results but the page text was not included in the evidence bundle, so sandbox/test-environment availability is unconfirmed.
Tables are Enterprise-only and there is no list-tables endpoint, so integrations must supply known table IDs.
The app name 'Clay' is ambiguous; it was disambiguated to the clay.com GTM data platform per the input hint, not other products named Clay.
